newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco cedes majority stake in Samir oil refinery.
newsitem.headline: Morocco cedes majority stake in Samir oil refinery.

text.p: Morocco ceded state majority stake in Samir firm refinery, the country's main oil refinery to Saudi Coral oil group, a Moroccan senior official said on Friday.

"The Moroccan government ceded its majority stake in Samir oil refinery...The agreement is on the verge to be finalised with Saudi coral oil group," the official, who declined to be named, told Reuters.
An official statement will be soon released and a news conference is expected to be held by Privatization Minister Abderrahman Saaidi on the issue next week, he said.
The official declined to give details of the Moroccan-Saudi deal, which concerns also the Societe Cherifienne des Petroles oil refinery.
Moroccan state holds 67 percent stake in Samir and 73.8 percent Societe Cherifienne des Petroles (SCP) firms.
According to a Casablanca-based market analyst, the deal is estimated at around $450 million.
Saaidi, who supervises directly the privatization operation of both oil firms, was not immediately available for comment.
The government floated 30 percent of Samir stocks on the Casablanca bourse at $310 million in March 1996.

Located in Mohammedia on the Atlantic coast, near Morocco's financial center of Casablanca, Societe Marocaine de l'Industrie du Raffinage (Samir) has capacity of six million tonnes per year, just over 120,000 barrels per day (bpd) and refines 80 percent of the country's domestic refined products.
One of largest market capitalisation firms, Samir has 20.64 million shares and an average daily trading volume of 3.32 million dirhams.
It made a net profit of 506 million dirhams ($53.2 million) and a turnover of 7.2 billion dirhams in 1996, Upline Securities stockbroker said.
SCP, which is the country's second refinery, processes the remaining 20 percent of Morocco's crude oil needs.
